_about: Chapter D (Determinism) of the suite results document: the prose data of DESIGN-DOC.md section 5 in R.json's format, written for the union of manifest v4 and v5 (the chapter's 21 scenarios, 1 family and 6 units are the same in both; v5's twins carry their sources' v5 requests and expectations, e.g. D-R-junction-0003's header runs, and property-level marks for the checks the tools do not expose). `summary` and `coverage_gap` lead the chapter page, `intro` follows the computed lines; `families` keys on the family id, `units` on the unit id. Every figure of the run is a placeholder (doc/facts.py) and every run-dependent sentence a conditional. The literal numbers are constants of the SPEC and of the manifest, listed under `_assumes`. Every claim follows SPEC-labeled-traversal-core.md section 6.8, SPEC-pattern-search.md section 7.9, areas.py gen_D, checks.py (check_deterministic, answer_digest) and service_by_design.json. The catalogue entry of `deterministic` is in checks.json; the twins' own checks are those of their sources' chapters (P, R, L, M, T, Q), catalogued there and in checks-QCND.json; the by-design cases it names: resolve.job_path (cases.json), pattern.not_expressible.max_steps (cases-QCND.json). Readability review (READ-320, READ-321, 2026-10-16): a `purpose` slot; the Background and the unit properties state the two dimensions apart (repeatability of the fields an access path exposes; the source property wherever its fields are exposed), the conclusion names the twin repeatable via MCP with its source property untested there (a conditional on the recorded standing), and D-P-scope-0004's detail block carries a `reading` line (`details`); the pairs tables of repeated tests print a three-repeat key and legend (cells.repeats_texts, READ-321); the later manifest's per-check marks are named as not exercised by a v4 run; every unit carries a reader-level `question`; access path replaces arm in the prose.

_assumes._note: The literal numbers this file's prose may carry, each with its source: constants of the SPEC, of the manifest (repeats, picks), of the service's table or of the harness, never a figure of a run (those are placeholders the generator fills). tests/test_doc.py fails on a number the prose carries that is listed neither here nor as a placeholder; add a constant here with its source, never a run's figure.

title: Determinism
purpose: A user who repeats a request wants the same answer, and the SPECs promise it wherever no time budget tripped. This chapter takes fast scenarios of six chapters and runs each three times on every access path, comparing the normalised answers' digests repeat by repeat and re-running the source's own checks. Its evidence is of I.2's fourth kind, consistency: equal digests show the answer repeating on that access path for the fields that path exposes, and nothing else; a source property is validated only where the fields its check reads are present.

intro: The SPECs promise that the same request answers the same: a traversal is deterministic provided no time budget tripped (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.8), a pattern search's answer repeats unless the entry states `determinism` `time_limited` (SPEC-pattern-search section 7.9), and a 503 deadline depends on the machine. Chapter D takes fast scenarios of the other chapters and runs each three times on every access path: P (six), R (four), L and M (three each), T and Q (two each), plus one complete planted search at `max_mismatches` 2, the forward planted window with the lowest chance estimate, so that it completes without a budget stop. The picks leave out everything whose answer may depend on what ran before it or on the clock: refusals, machine-dependent and retention-dependent scenarios, relation twins, split cases, warm-ups, run-unique attempt ids, raw bodies and custom headers, and any status expectation other than a 200.

A twin keeps its source's request and property checks (its status expectation replaced by a 200) and adds `deterministic`: the answer's digest, the sha256 of the canonical JSON of the normalised answer without its headers and timing keys, must equal the digests of the earlier repeats on the same access path that no time budget limited; the first repeat has nothing to compare and rests on the other checks, a time-limited repeat reads inconclusive unless its stated limitation cannot have happened (appendix A). So a twin shows two things, to be read apart: on every access path, the repeatability of the fields that path exposes (the digests equal across the repeats; the pairs tables mark each row = or ≠), and, wherever the fields the source's checks read are exposed, the source's property passing each time. Via MCP the tool's answer omits some host fields, so a source check that reads an omitted field is not exposed there: the MCP digests then show the service's projection repeating, which validates nothing about the omitted field. The record key of each source is in its own chapter.

Via MCP each repeat is a new search or job: the MCP runner names an idempotency key per execution, so the service's reuse of a running or recent identical search (`service.pattern_repeat_reuses_search`, appendix B) does not apply, and a resolve is a new job on the anonymous path (`resolve.job_path`, `service.resolve_repeat`). The tool's answer carries the fields the service exposes, so a source check that reads a field the service drops is not exposed on that access path [[manifest_version >= 5 ? (this manifest marks these per check) | (this run's manifest, version 4, carries no such mark: the check itself records the missing field as not exposed; a later manifest version marks these per check, which this run does not exercise)]], and the MCP digests compare the tool's answers with one another, never with the direct access paths' documents. A source naming a field the tool cannot send (`max_steps`: `pattern.not_expressible.max_steps`) is !!not exercised there!!.

D.title: determinism
D.prose: One family, six units by the source's chapter. Each twin's three repeats on an access path must answer the same digest, and the source's own checks must pass on each: a 12-mer counted in suffix scope, a 25-mer's contexts at their offsets, a window placed under a predicate, the first 20 bases of lambda in suffix scope, a 25-mer with three IUPAC codes and a random 31-mer absent (D-P); a window resolved under its column at one k-mer, 100 bp and 2,000 bp, and the junction of two records (D-R); a 32 bp path search, a 40 bp record-verified path and a supported path at the label_intersection level (D-L); a planted search out of reach (two substitutions at `max_mismatches` 1), an IUPAC search with one substitution, a `max_steps` stop in partial with its cut, and the complete planted search at `max_mismatches` 2 (D-M); a 31 bp seed walked right under its header and a seed with its derived carrier set (D-T); `any(A)` selecting the record's contexts and the `-` source contexts selected under context strands (D-Q). D.claim: the same request answers the same digest three times on every access path that exercised it, and its source's property holds each time on the direct access paths, where every field its checks read is exposed

D-P.property: Three repeats of a chapter P source (a 12-mer counted in suffix scope, a 25-mer's contexts, a window placed under a predicate, a suffix-scope search, three IUPAC codes, a random 31-mer absent) answer the same digest on every access path (deterministic: the fields that path exposes repeat), and the source's own checks pass each time where that path exposes the fields they read.
D-P.question: Do three repeats of a /pattern source answer the same digest on each access path, and does the source's own check pass each time where its fields are exposed?
D-P.note: The source property of a twin is validated only where its field is in the answer: a source check that reads a field the tool's answer omits is not exposed via MCP, and the twin is then repeatable there without that property being tested there (the detail block of such a twin says which field).

D-R.property: Three repeats of a chapter R source (a window resolved under its column at one k-mer, 100 bp and 2,000 bp; a junction) answer the same digest on every access path (deterministic: the fields that path exposes repeat), and the source's own checks pass each time where that path exposes the fields they read.
D-R.question: Do three repeats of a /resolve source answer the same digest on each access path, and does the source's own check pass each time where its fields are exposed?

D-L.question: Do three repeats of a long-pattern source answer the same digest on each access path, and does the source's own check pass each time where its fields are exposed?

D-M.property: Three repeats of a chapter M source (a planted search out of reach at max_mismatches 1, an IUPAC search with one substitution, a max_steps stop in partial, a complete planted search at max_mismatches 2) answer the same digest on every access path (deterministic: the fields that path exposes repeat), and the source's own checks pass each time where that path exposes the fields they read.
D-M.question: Do three repeats of a mismatch source answer the same digest on each access path, and does the source's own check pass each time where its fields are exposed?

D-T.property: Three repeats of a chapter T source (a 31 bp seed walked under its header, a seed with its derived carrier set) answer the same digest on every access path (deterministic: the fields that path exposes repeat), and the source's own checks pass each time where that path exposes the fields they read.
D-T.question: Do three repeats of a /traverse source answer the same digest on each access path, and does the source's own check pass each time where its fields are exposed?

D-Q.question: Do three repeats of a predicate source answer the same digest on each access path, and does the source's own check pass each time where its fields are exposed?
